notes:
This is a minor release: watched folders can include subfolders, and the review surface adds accessibility and Windows preference support. Existing settings, export formats, and review workflows remain compatible.

FEATURES
• Watched folders can include subfolders. New images anywhere below the watch are collected; images already in nested folders count as ready and can be queued with PROCESS EXISTING.
• Saved copies from a recursive watch repeat the source's subfolders under `redacted`, so exports keep their folder structure and are less likely to collide.
• A watched folder can no longer sit inside another watched folder. Use Include subfolders on the parent, or watch the child by itself.

ENHANCEMENTS
• Review boxes expose accessible names and state to screen readers. Folder and inbox rows name their status and counts.
• The Method control has a visible keyboard focus ring, and compact controls have larger vertical hit areas.
• MarkSeal follows Windows text size up to 110%, reduced-motion, and high-contrast preferences at launch. High contrast uses a system palette and overrides theme choices.
• Selected boxes show a check mark, excluded boxes show a dash, and a dark keyline keeps the boundary visible on light screenshots.
• The confirmed-image caption keeps the filename and method visible on narrow windows and groups Rule tags, Copy image, and Verify under Actions.
• Watched-folder and blocked-pattern settings save immediately; those tabs show Close instead of Cancel and hide Apply.
• Empty and ready states name the next step more directly, and recovery messages explain what to do after a failure.

FIXES
• Closing MarkSeal with unsaved review work asks before discarding it.
• The error banner settles into view instead of appearing over the caption.
• The status board uses tabular figures and a staggered flip so count changes settle in sequence.

OPTIMIZATIONS
• Changing a box no longer reloads the image.
• Detection suggestions are assembled in one pass, so category and box handling now runs in one place.

The Windows installer remains unsigned; Windows may show an unknown-publisher warning. Linux and macOS builds are produced in CI without running the test suite on those platforms.
